docs.title: AnimateService
docs.text:
Stock Animate was built for obbies in 2014 — not high-speed anime combat.

AnimateService completely takes over character animation. Your combat systems, skill movesets, emote wheels, cutscenes and downslams all talk to it through a typed signal bus (AnimSignals). No other script ever touches Animator:LoadAnimation() directly.

flowchart LR
    CB[Combat / Skills / Emotes] --> BUS[AnimSignals<br/>typed signal bus]
    BUS --> SVC[AnimateService<br/>client service]
    SVC --> AN[Character Animator]
    SVC --> CP[ContentProvider<br/>asset cache]

No other script loads animations. Ever. That's the whole deal.

docs.title: Why you'll love it
docs.text:
The stock Animate trap How AnimateService fixes it Blind LoadAnimation every swing (leaked tracks) LoadedBin registry — every track indexed by clean ID and reused First-swing frame hitch (asset fetch mid-combo) System-side PreloadAsync — first play and replays dispatch in ~0.1ms Marker callbacks dropped on cache hit Marker fanout — N systems listen to Hit / CanCancel on the same track Zero clean stop path StopCategoryTrack & StopAllInCategory — feints, interrupts, stuns cancel cleanly Tracks leak across lives Per-life lifecycle — old tracks die on death, asset cache stays warm Locomotion stomps combat arms Caller-typed priority — pass what each move needs, or clamp combat to Action2+ Default Animate fights your scripts Instant suppression — empty StarterCharacterScripts/Animate kills stock at the root

Measured live in Play Solo (10-slot core): 10 tracks on spawn, 10 after respawn — never 20, never 38. Cold fetch ~125.9ms, preloaded dispatch ~0.1ms.

docs.title: 60-second tour
docs.text:
1. Drop Module/, Services/, Libraries/ into StarterPlayerScripts.
  2. Delete stock Animate (empty Animate LocalScript suppresses it).
  3. Fire a signal:
local AnimSignals = require(game.StarterPlayer.StarterPlayerScripts.Libraries.AnimSignals)

AnimSignals.PlayCategoryTrack:Fire("M1", "rbxassetid://123456789", {
    FadeTime = 0.05,
    Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action2,
})

That's it. The track loads once, replays forever at 0.1ms, and dies cleanly with your character.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
New here? Follow the fun path:

Quickstart → Life of a Swing → Combat Recipes

Or jump around:

  • Architecture — signal bus, LoadedBin, locomotion state machine
  • Priority & Partial-Body — why Action beats Core for combat arms
  • Signal Catalog — every signal, every payload
  • Module Mode — same engine, require instead of signals
  • Tests — 9 proofs you can run in Studio right now

docs.title: Adding Animations
docs.text: Three places, three jobs. Don't mix them up.

docs.title: 1. Locomotion (under the launcher)
docs.text:
Add R15Animations / R6Animations folders — or stock-style StringValue slots — as children of Services/AnimateService. Discovered per spawn by rig type.

Slots: Idle, Walk, Run, Sprint, Jump, Fall, Climb, Swim, SwimIdle, Sit.

No source at all = combat-only mode. Legal.

Module mode alternatives (see Config):

  • CoreFolder → any folder holding those structures.
  • CoreProfile = { Idle = "rbxassetid://…", Walk = … } (wins over folders).
  • CoreResolver = function(humanoid) … end (pick by rig type or player data).

docs.title: 2. Combat (just asset IDs)
docs.text:
Keep your own table of M1s, dashes and reactions (see Tests/TestKit.luau for the shape) and dispatch by ID:

local MOVES = {
    M1_1 = "rbxassetid://123456789",
    M1_2 = "rbxassetid://123456790",
    Dash = "rbxassetid://123456791",
}

AnimSignals.PlayCategoryTrack:Fire("M1", MOVES.M1_1, {
    FadeTime = 0.05,
    Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action2,
})

Character-specific tables override per slot and fall back to shared defaults. Omitted Priority loads at Core — pass Action2+ for combat.

Partial-body rule: hands-only clips (upper torso + arms + head keyed, legs unkeyed) at Action+ give you walk-while-blocking. Full-body clips at Core fight locomotion. See Priority.

docs.title: 3. Preload before the fight
docs.text:
-- loading screen / round start / entering combat
AnimSignals.PreloadAnims:Fire({ Ids = { MOVES.M1_1, MOVES.M1_2, MOVES.Dash } })

-- equip a moveset without playing (registers into the bin)
AnimSignals.LoadBatch:Fire({ Ids = { MOVES.M1_1, MOVES.M1_2 }, Category = "M1" })

LoadBatch only takes flat ID lists — it can't name a profile. Use LoadProfile for that.

Assets are per-owner

Clips you upload only load in experiences you own (or that the asset is shared with). The tests use Roblox's public defaults so they run anywhere.

docs.title: Architecture & Data Flow
docs.text:
Everything funnels through one door. Your game never touches the Animator directly.

flowchart TD
    subgraph Gameplay ["Game Systems (Combat, Skills, Emotes, Cutscenes)"]
        CB["CombatController / SkillService"]
        FX["VFX / SFX Listeners"]
    end

    subgraph Bus ["AnimSignals (Typed Signal Bus)"]
        S1["PlayCategoryTrack"]
        S2["StopCategoryTrack / StopAllInCategory"]
        S3["BindMarker"]
        S4["PlayOneOff"]
        S5["PreloadAnims / LoadBatch"]
        S6["SetCoreProfile"]
    end

    subgraph Core ["AnimateService (Local Client Service)"]
        BIN["LoadedBin & Deduplicator (_byId)"]
        WATCH["Playing-count watchdog (engine cap 64)"]
        FAN["Marker Fanout Engine"]
        LOCO["Locomotion State Machine (Speed & Rig Scale)"]
    end

    subgraph Engine ["Roblox Engine"]
        AN["Character Animator"]
        CP["ContentProvider (Persistent Asset Cache)"]
    end

    CB --> Bus
    CB -.->|"direct calls (module mode)"| Core
    FX -.->|Listen to markers| Bus
    Bus --> Core
    Core --> AN
    Core --> CP

docs.title: The four boxes
docs.text:
1. LoadedBin & Deduplicator (_byId) — every combat track indexed by clean ID. Same ID under two categories shares one track. Never loaded twice per life. See Core Concepts.

2. Playing-count watchdog — loading is free (200/200 LoadAnimation calls succeed). Playing is budgeted: the engine refuses past 64 active tracks per Animator. The service warns past 48 (5s throttle) — headroom for anything else on the rig. OneOffs auto-destroy, death wipes the bin.

3. Marker fanout — one native connection per (track, marker), N listeners via task.spawn. Hitbox + shake + SFX all hear "hitreg".

4. Locomotion state machine — Humanoid state + speed → exactly one core track (Idle, Walk, Run, Sprint, Jump, Fall, Climb, Swim, SwimIdle, Sit). Speed dividends (Walk/16, Run/18, Sprint/22, Climb/12, Swim/16) and rig-scale normalisation included.

docs.title: Combat signal & marker flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Combat as Combat System
    actor VFX as Effects Listener
    participant Bus as AnimSignals
    participant Svc as AnimateService
    participant Track as AnimationTrack

    VFX->>Bus: BindMarker("OneOff", downslamId, "hitreg", spawnRubble)
    Combat->>Bus: PlayOneOff(downslamId, { FadeTime = 0.05 })
    Bus->>Svc: LoadCategory("OneOff", downslamId)
    Svc->>Track: Play(0.05)
    Note over Track: Animation reaches "hitreg" keyframe
    Track-->>Svc: GetMarkerReachedSignal("hitreg")
    Svc->>VFX: spawnRubble(coords) [task.spawn fanout]
    Note over Track: Clip ends
    Track-->>Svc: Stopped event
    Svc->>Track: Destroy() & unregister from LoadedBin

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
Module/AnimateService       -- the engine (single implementation)
Services/AnimateService     -- launcher: Configure + Init + Start
Libraries/AnimSignals       -- 12 typed signals (the bus)
Libraries/Signal            -- SignalPlus v3.7.2, vendored
Tests/                      -- 9 proofs, run one at a time

Module/AnimateService is the implementation. Services/AnimateService only calls Configure, Init, Start on it. Mix signal fires and direct require calls freely — same code either way.

docs.title: Benchmarks
docs.text: Numbers measured live in Play Solo on a 10-slot core. Your counts follow your folders — the behaviours hold for any setup.

docs.title: The headline
docs.text:
• Initial core: exactly 10 tracks on spawn.
  • Zero leak on respawn: rebuilds 10. Never 20, never 38.
  • Cold vs warm: un-preloaded fetch ~125.9ms, preloaded dispatch ~0.1ms.
  • Reuse flat: PlayCategoryTrack on a loaded ID stays 10 → 11 → 11. Zero allocations.
[Validator] PASS single reuse second load flat -- before 10 mid 11 after 11
[PartialTest] CONFIRMED old track dead after respawn: parentNil=true replayOk=true
[PartialTest] same id dispatches in 0.1ms after respawn (content cached, only the track is new)

docs.title: Replay without re-loading (same life)
docs.text:
Loading an already-loaded animation reuses the existing AnimationTrack. Count stays flat:

[Validator] PASS single reuse second load flat -- before 10 mid 11 after 11

First load 10 → 11. Second load 11 → 11.

docs.title: The two caches
docs.text:
• ContentProvider:PreloadAsync() — downloads bytes from Roblox's cloud. Creates zero tracks.
  • LoadedBin — maps an AnimationTrack on your Animator.

If your loading screen already preloaded the IDs, PlayCategoryTrack lands in under 0.1ms with no hitch.

docs.title: Across death
docs.text:
[PartialTest] CONFIRMED old track dead after respawn: parentNil=true replayOk=true
  • parentNil = true — old track detached and destroyed.
  • replayOk = true — the engine doesn't throw on :Play() of a dead track; it fails silently. (Don't hoard tracks.)
  • 0.1ms — asset bytes survive, only the track is new.

docs.title: Watchdog math
docs.text:
• Engine cap: 64 active tracks per Animator (down from 256). Past it, new plays are refused.
  • Service warn: 48 concurrent playing (5s throttle) — headroom for anything else on the rig.
  • 200/200 loads succeed — loading isn't capped, so load your whole moveset. Budget plays, not loads.

Run the proofs: Tests — AnimValidator (reuse + respawn), AnimStutterTest (cold vs warm), AnimOneOffTest (warm OneOff + auto-unload).

docs.title: Core Concepts
docs.text: Seven ideas. Learn these and the API is obvious.

docs.title: 1. Locomotion core profiles
docs.text:
Full suites: Idle, Walk, Run, Sprint, Jump, Fall, Climb, Swim, SwimIdle, Sit, ToolNone.

  • Adaptive speed dividends — playback matches movement speed: Walk /16, Run /18, Sprint /22, Climb /12, Swim /16.
  • Rig-scale aware — with ApplyRigScale = true, velocity is normalised by Character:GetScale(). Giant bosses stop moonwalking.
  • Profile swapping — SetCoreProfile("Injured") swaps the whole suite instantly (warrior → ninja → limp). Must be loaded first via LoadProfile or ExtraProfiles.

docs.title: 2. LoadedBin & global dedup (_byId)
docs.text:
Every track enters the bin, keyed by clean ID (rbxassetid://123 ↔ 123):

  • System A loads m1_combo1 as "M1", system B wants it as "Single" — they share the exact same track.
  • Never loaded twice on the same life. Second load is flat: 10 → 11 → 11.

docs.title: 3. Singles vs OneOffs
docs.text:
• Kept Singles (M1s, dashes, blocks, skills) — loaded once, replayed at ~0.1ms, kept across StopCategoryTrack. For moves used repeatedly.
  • OneOffs (cutscenes, awakenings, downslams) — auto-disconnect markers and :Destroy() the instant Stopped fires. Zero footprint. Fire-and-forget.

docs.title: 4. Playing-cap watchdog
docs.text:
Loads are free, plays are budgeted:

  • 200/200 LoadAnimation calls succeed — loading isn't capped.
  • Playing is: the engine refuses past 64 active tracks per Animator (down from 256).
  • So the service guards the right thing: no cap on loaded, warn past 48 concurrent playing (5s throttle) — headroom for anything else on the rig.
  • OneOffs auto-destroy, death wipes the bin.

docs.title: 5. Marker fanout
docs.text:
Native :GetMarkerReachedSignal() allows one connection per track without plumbing, and breaks on reload.

  • OnMarker() creates one native connection and fans out to N listeners via task.spawn.
  • Hit detection, shake, sound and particles all hook "hitreg" independently.
  • Listeners live on the track → die with the character. Rebind each life, ideally right before you play.
  • OnMarker returns a handle with Disconnect(). ClearMarkers drops every listener on a marker — or the whole clip when you omit the name. Use it when a move is cancelled.

docs.title: 6. Death & respawn
docs.text:
• Tracks die with the character (Parent == nil).
  • The stale-reference trap: calling :Play() on a dead track throws no error — silent fail. Never hold raw tracks; dispatch by ID.
  • Asset data stays warm in ContentProvider, so 10 core tracks rebuild in under a millisecond.
  • Remembered: loaded profiles, active core (unless PersistProfiles = false), preload cache. Forgotten: tracks, marker listeners, active overlay (definition remembered — re-arm it).

docs.title: 7. One-shots end for everyone
docs.text:
A non-looped track that finishes only ends locally. Without an explicit Stop, other clients freeze on its last frame.

Every non-looped category track gets an Ended → Stop(0.05) hook automatically. Playback is never cut short (markers, hit windows, tail frames all run) and the end replicates after. On by default, nothing to call.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Small words, big consequences. Skim this once — it'll save you a jittery afternoon.

Term What it means Single A kept combat track (M1, Skill, Block). Loaded once, replayed forever, survives Stop. Dies only on death. OneOff A fire-and-forget clip (PlayOneOff). Auto-Destroy()s on Stopped. Zero footprint. Cutscenes, downslams, awakenings. LoadedBin The per-life track registry (_categories + _byId). Every loaded track lives here, keyed by clean ID. Clean ID Normalised asset ID (rbxassetid://123 ↔ 123). Dedup key — same clip under two categories shares one track. _byId Global dedup map inside the bin. If system A loads m1_combo1 as "M1" and system B wants it as "Single", they get the same track. Core profile A full locomotion suite (Idle, Walk, Run, …). Replaces locomotion when activated via SetCoreProfile. Overlay An arms-layer set that plays on top of the active core (dagger stance, weapon guard). Legs fall through to core. Marker A named keyframe ("Hit", "Impact", "hitreg"). Hook N callbacks via BindMarker / OnMarker. Fanout One native GetMarkerReachedSignal connection, N listeners via task.spawn. Everyone hears the marker. Watchdog Playing-cap guard. Loads are free (200/200 succeed); plays are budgeted (engine cap 64, warn at 48). Stale reference A raw AnimationTrack held across respawn. Its Parent is nil and :Play() fails silently. Dispatch by ID instead. Ended hook Auto Ended → Stop(0.05) on every non-looped category track, so one-shots end for everyone, not just you. Clamp ClampCombatPriority = true forces combat tracks to Action2–Action4. Anything lower becomes Action2. Training wheels for combat games. Rig The per-life controller (AnimateService.Rig). Owns one character's Animator, profiles, bin and state machine. Rig.new(model) works on any Humanoid rig.

docs.title: The two caches (don't mix them up)
docs.text:
• ContentProvider:PreloadAsync() — downloads keyframe bytes from Roblox's cloud to your client. Creates zero tracks.
  • LoadedBin — maps an AnimationTrack already loaded onto your Animator.

Rule of thumb: if your loading screen already preloaded the IDs, PlayCategoryTrack lands in under 0.1ms with no hitch.

docs.title: Life of a Swing
docs.text: Follow one M1 from button press to second swing. This is the mental model for everything else.

docs.title: Act 1: The press
docs.text:
You press LMB. Your CombatController doesn't touch the Animator — it fires a signal:

AnimSignals.PlayCategoryTrack:Fire("M1", M1_ID, {
    FadeTime = 0.05,
    Speed = 1.1,
    Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action2,
})

AutoPlay defaults to true here. Pass AutoPlay = false and it only loads.

docs.title: Act 2: The lookup (three doors)
docs.text:
Inside Rig:LoadCategory, the service normalises your ID (rbxassetid://123 ↔ 123) and checks three doors in order:

  1. Same-bucket hit — M1/123 already loaded? Bump Refs, re-apply Priority / Looped, hook any MarkerName, Play() or AdjustSpeed(). Zero allocations.
  2. Cross-category share — another system loaded 123 under "Single"? Alias the exact same track into M1. Never loaded twice per life.
  3. Fresh load — Instance.new("Animation") + Animator:LoadAnimation() + register in both bucket and _byId. Then Play(0.05) and run the playing-cap watchdog.
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Absent
    Absent --> Preloaded: PreloadAnims / ContentProvider
    Preloaded --> Loaded: LoadCategory (Single / kept track)
    Loaded --> Playing: PlayCategoryTrack / PlaySingle
    Playing --> Stopped: StopCategoryTrack / natural end
    Stopped --> Playing: Instant replay (~0.1ms)
    Playing --> OneOffEnded: PlayOneOff clip finishes
    OneOffEnded --> Absent: Auto-destroys track
    Loaded --> Absent: Character death (full wipe)
    note right of Absent: Death wipes tracks.\nContentProvider cache survives.

docs.title: Act 3: The markers
docs.text:
Mid-swing your hitbox needs to fire exactly on the "Hit" keyframe. Somewhere else — maybe at startup, maybe right before the swing — someone bound it:

AnimSignals.BindMarker:Fire("M1", M1_ID, "Hit", function()
    DamageService:CastHitbox()
end)

The service keeps one native GetMarkerReachedSignal("Hit") connection and fans out to every listener via task.spawn. Hit detection, screen shake, sound and particles can all hook the same marker independently. It survives reuse because the listener lives on the track entry, not the load call.

docs.title: Act 4: The feint
docs.text:
You press Q to dash-cancel mid-windup:

AnimSignals.StopCategoryTrack:Fire("M1", M1_ID, 0.05)

Omit the ID and the whole M1 bucket stops. Got parried instead? Nuke it:

AnimSignals.StopAllInCategory:Fire({ Category = "M1", Fade = 0.05 })

Kept Singles stay in the bin after stop — replay is instant. OneOffs (PlayOneOff) are different: they Destroy() themselves the moment Stopped fires. Fire-and-forget.

docs.title: Act 5: The second swing
docs.text:
You swing again. Same ID, same bucket. Door #1 hits. Track count stays flat:

[Validator] PASS single reuse second load flat -- before 10 mid 11 after 11

First load 10 → 11. Second load 11 → 11. That's dedup working.

docs.title: Act 6: Death
docs.text:
You die. Every track on your old Animator is now a dead instance (Parent == nil). Calling :Play() on one fails silently — no error, just nothing. That's the stale-reference trap.

So don't hold tracks. Dispatch by ID every time:

  • Remembered across lives: loaded profiles, active core (unless PersistProfiles = false), preload cache.
  • Forgotten: tracks, marker listeners, active overlay (definition remembered — just re-arm it).

Respawn rebuilds your 10 core tracks warm in under a millisecond, because ContentProvider still has the bytes:

[PartialTest] same id dispatches in 0.1ms after respawn (content cached, only the track is new)

docs.title: The one-sentence version
docs.text:
Preload like you mean it, dispatch by ID, never hoard tracks past death.

Next: Priority & Partial-Body — why your block needs Action, not Core.

docs.title: Death & Respawn
docs.text: Death is a feature. Here's exactly what survives and what doesn't.

docs.title: What happens
docs.text:
1. Humanoid.Died → state Dead → all core + overlay tracks stop.
  2. New character spawns → old Rig:Destroy() (disconnect all, Stop(0) + Destroy every track).
  3. New Rig.new(character) → preload core + persisted + extra IDs → LoadProfile("__Default__") → replay persisted profiles → activate remembered core → Init() + Start().

Because ContentProvider still holds the bytes, the rebuild is warm:

[PartialTest] same id dispatches in 0.1ms after respawn (content cached, only the track is new)

docs.title: Remembered vs forgotten
docs.text: Remembered across lives Forgotten (rebuild it) Loaded profiles + active core (unless PersistProfiles = false) Tracks (Parent == nil now) Overlay definitions Active overlay (re-arm by name) Preload cache (ContentProvider) Marker listeners ExtraProfiles (reloaded every life) Raw AnimationTrack references in your code

docs.title: The stale-reference trap
docs.text:
-- DON'T do this:
local track = AnimService:GetTrack("M1", M1_ID)
-- ... player dies ...
track:Play() -- no error, silent nothing. You're animating a corpse.

Always dispatch by ID:

-- DO this:
AnimSignals.PlayCategoryTrack:Fire("M1", M1_ID, { Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action2 })

docs.title: Between lives
docs.text:
There is no rig between lives. Play, stop and marker calls made then are dropped (return nil). Profiles, overlay definitions and Preload are remembered.

Use readiness helpers to act once a rig exists:

local AnimateService = require(path.to.Module.AnimateService)

-- yield until spawn (optional timeout)
local rig = AnimateService:WaitForRig(10)

-- or subscribe (fires now if a rig exists, again every respawn)
local conn = AnimateService:OnRigReady(function(rig)
    AnimSignals.LoadOverlay:Fire({
        Profile = "DaggerArms",
        Definition = DAGGER_ARMS,
        SetActive = true,
        Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action,
    })
end)
-- conn:Disconnect() when done

Re-arm overlays per life

Overlay definitions survive, but the active overlay doesn't. OnRigReady is the perfect place to re-arm it.

docs.title: Never cache
docs.text:
• Never cache the rig across respawn — ask GetRig() again.
  • Never cache a track across respawn — ask by (category, id) again.
  • LoadProfile with an existing name is ignored — use ReplaceProfile to swap contents.

docs.title: Limits & Roadmap
docs.text: No surprises. What's true today, and what's next.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• No eviction. Kept Singles stay loaded until death. Keep and per-entry LastUsed / Refs are recorded but nothing reads them yet.
  • Signals aren't queued. A fire before the bus connects — or between lives — is lost. Profiles, overlay defs and Preload are remembered; play/stop/marker with no rig are dropped.
  • Markers + active overlay don't survive respawn. Rebind / re-arm each life (OnRigReady is your friend).
  • Server NPC rigs via AnimateService.Rig.new(model) should work but are untested.
  • Assets are per-owner. Uploads only load where you own (or share) them. Tests use public defaults so they run anywhere.

docs.title: Roadmap ideas
docs.text:
• Optional eviction (LRU on LastUsed / Refs) for giant movesets.
  • Queued early fires (or explicit WaitForReady bus) so top-level fires stop vanishing.
  • First-class NPC rig support + server tests.
  • Overlay persistence option (remember active overlay, not just definitions).

PRs welcome — keep the bin flat and the dispatches warm.

docs.title: Markers & Fanout
docs.text: Keyframes your whole game can hear. One native connection, N listeners.

docs.title: The problem with raw markers
docs.text: Roblox's :GetMarkerReachedSignal() gives you one connection per track without manual plumbing — and it breaks when tracks reload. Two systems wanting "Hit" on the same swing step on each other.

docs.title: What the service does
docs.text:
OnMarker() creates one native connection per (track, marker) and fans out to every listener via task.spawn:

  • Hit detection, screen shake, sound and particles all hook "hitreg" independently.
  • Works on kept Singles and OneOffs.
  • Listeners live on the track → die with the character. Rebind each life, ideally right before you play.
-- hitbox + shake on the same marker, no conflict
AnimSignals.BindMarker:Fire("Skill", SKILL_ID, "Hit", function()
    DamageService:CastHitbox()
end)

AnimSignals.BindMarker:Fire("Skill", SKILL_ID, "Hit", function()
    CameraShaker:Shake(CameraShaker.Presets.HeavyExplosion)
end)

Direct mode returns a handle:

local handle = AnimateService:OnMarker("Skill", SKILL_ID, "Hit", onHit)
-- later:
handle:Disconnect() -- removes just this listener

OnMarker lazy-loads: bind on a never-loaded ID and it loads (AutoPlay = false) then hooks. No throw.

docs.title: Clearing
docs.text:
-- drop every listener on one marker (e.g. swing cancelled)
AnimateService:ClearMarkers("M1", M1_ID, "Hit")

-- drop the whole clip's listeners
AnimateService:ClearMarkers("M1", M1_ID)

-- via signals
AnimSignals.ClearMarkers:Fire({ Category = "M1", AnimId = M1_ID, Marker = "Hit" })
AnimSignals.ClearMarkers:Fire({ Category = "M1", AnimId = M1_ID })

Use it when a move is feinted or interrupted.

docs.title: Shorthand during load
docs.text:
AnimSignals.PlayCategoryTrack:Fire("Skill", SKILL_ID, {
    FadeTime = 0.1,
    Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action3,
    MarkerName = "Hit",
    MarkerCallback = function() DamageService:CastHitbox() end,
    OnLoaded = function(track)
        track:AdjustSpeed(1.2)
    end,
})

docs.title: You need a marked clip to test
docs.text: Marker checks need a clip that actually contains a marker. Set MarkerClip (and MarkerName) in Tests/TestKit.luau — otherwise those checks print SKIP and the rubble demo stays quiet. AnimMarkerTest covers bookkeeping without any marked clip.

docs.title: Module Mode
docs.text:
Same engine, driven by require instead of signals. Module/AnimateService is the single implementation; Services/AnimateService only calls Configure, Init, Start on it.

Mix both styles freely — a signal fire and a direct call reach the same code.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
local AnimateService = require(path.to.Module.AnimateService)

AnimateService:Configure({ ClampCombatPriority = true })
AnimateService:Init()
AnimateService:Start()

Init then Start matches ModuleLoader-style services. With a loader, put Module/AnimateService in a client Services folder and let the loader run it.

Configure can run any time, but the first life reads it during Start, and UseSignals / Signals / Debug are read once at Start. With a loader, call it from another module's Init, or edit the defaults in the file.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
Same verbs as the signals — call with a colon:

Group Methods Playback PlayCategory(category, animId, opts?) loads + plays (AutoPlay = false = load only), returns track. PlayOneOff(animId, opts?), StopCategory(category, animId?, fade?), StopAllCategory(category, fade?) Markers OnMarker(category, animId, marker, cb) → MarkerHandle with Disconnect(). ClearMarkers(category, animId, marker?) Queries GetTrack, IsPlaying, GetLoadedCount, GetLoadedList, GetDebugInfo, SetLocomotionWeight(mult) Profiles SetCoreProfile(name), LoadProfile(name, def, setActive?), ReplaceProfile(name, def), LoadOverlay(name, def, setActive?, priority?), SetOverlayProfile(name?, priority?), ClearOverlay() Preload Preload(ids) needs no character — call from a loading screen. LoadBatch(ids, category?, keep?) Readiness IsReady(), GetRig(), WaitForRig(timeout?), OnRigReady(cb) (fires now if a rig exists + every respawn, returns SignalPlus Connection) Lifecycle Configure, Init, Start, Shutdown

docs.title: Rules of thumb
docs.text:
• Between lives there is no rig. Play/stop/marker calls are dropped (nil). Profiles, overlay defs and Preload are remembered. Use WaitForRig() or OnRigReady(cb).
  • Never cache the rig or a track across respawn — ask GetRig() again.
  • LoadProfile with an existing name is ignored. Use ReplaceProfile to swap contents.

docs.title: Client only, rigs anywhere
docs.text:
The controller owns the LocalPlayer's character, so on the server Init warns and does nothing. The per-rig class it wraps works on any Humanoid rig:

local rig = AnimateService.Rig.new(model)
rig:LoadProfile("__Default__", def)
rig:SetActiveProfile("__Default__")
rig:Init()
rig:Start()
-- later: rig:Destroy()

Driving server-side NPC rigs this way should work but is untested.

Full reference: Controller API · Rig API · Config

docs.title: Priority & The Partial-Body Rule
docs.text:
Roblox blends animations per joint, high to low. Each joint adds weights top-down until the sum hits 1.0 — then lower tracks are skipped for that joint.

Same priority blends by weight (normalised past 1.0). Two Core tracks on one joint average out instead of one winning — that's the "hiccup".

flowchart TB
    A4["Action4 — Stun / Ragdoll / Knockback / Death"]
    A3["Action3 — Skills / Blocks / Getting Hit / OneOff Finishers"]
    A2["Action2 — M1 Combos / Dashes / Emotes"]
    MV["Movement — Walk / Run / Sprint / Climb / Swim / Fall"]
    CR["Core — Idle / Seated / ToolNone"]

    A4 --> A3 --> A2 --> MV --> CR

docs.title: The table (pin this)
docs.text:
Enum Value Typical usage Idle 0 Character idle Movement 1 Walk, run, swim, climb, locomotion Action 2 Actions overriding idle + locomotion Action2 3 Overrides Action (M1s, dashes, emotes) Action3 4 Overrides Action2 (skills, blocks, hits, OneOffs) Action4 5 Highest (stun, ragdoll, death) Core 1000 Lowest — default when Priority is omitted

Core looks big, acts small

Core = 1000 reads like the highest number. The engine treats it as the lowest priority. Omit Priority and your combat clip loads at Core — underneath locomotion. That's almost never what you want for a swing.

docs.title: The Deepwoken rule
docs.text:
Hands at Action2+, legs free.

Make blocking or m1_combo1 with keyframes only on upper torso, arms and head. Leave lower torso and legs unkeyed. Unkeyed joints fall through — legs keep playing whatever runs below.

Eyeball test from AnimPartialTest (run it yourself with WASD):

  • blocking at Action — run around, legs sprint freely, arms locked in guard. Correct!
  • blocking at Core — locomotion fights the guard, glitchy jittering mess. Wrong!

Guidance (measured): hands-only clips look right above locomotion and wrong at its level. Pass Action+ for combat.

docs.title: How the service applies it
docs.text:
By default the service assigns nothing to category tracks: omitted Priority loads at Core. Pass any Enum.AnimationPriority and it loads at that instead.

A combat game that keeps combat above locomotion:

AnimateService:Configure({
    LocomotionPriority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Movement,
    ClampCombatPriority = true, -- force combat to Action2+
    DefaultOverlayPriority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action,
})

With ClampCombatPriority = true, category tracks may only be Action2–Action4. Anything lower (including Core or nil) becomes MinCombatPriority (Action2).

Locomotion at Movement

Default locomotion loads at Core. Set LocomotionPriority = Movement and stray Core clips stop stomping your walk cycle. The stack diagram above assumes you did.

docs.title: Profiles & Overlays
docs.text:
Two layers, one rule: core replaces, overlay stacks.

base core (__Default__) < overlay (arms, Action) < combat (M1/Skill, Action2+)

docs.title: Core profiles
docs.text:
Full locomotion suites (Idle, Walk, Run, …). Activate one at a time.

-- load + activate immediately
AnimSignals.LoadProfile:Fire({
    Profile = "Injured",
    Definition = {
        Idle = "rbxassetid://...",
        Walk = "rbxassetid://...",
        Run = "rbxassetid://...",
    },
    SetActive = true, -- default true; false = load only
})

-- swap later (must be loaded first)
AnimSignals.SetCoreProfile:Fire({ Profile = "Injured" })
AnimSignals.SetCoreProfile:Fire({ Profile = "__Default__" }) -- back to spawn suite

Module mode:

AnimateService:LoadProfile("Injured", INJURED_DEF, true)
AnimateService:SetCoreProfile("Injured")
AnimateService:ReplaceProfile("Injured", NEW_DEF) -- swap contents of an existing name

Preload suites so SetCoreProfile never waits:

AnimateService:Configure({
    ExtraProfiles = { Injured = INJURED_DEF, Ninja = NINJA_DEF },
})

Loaded profiles and the active core survive respawns (unless PersistProfiles = false).

docs.title: Overlays
docs.text:
Arms-only sets that play on top of whatever core is active. Legs fall through to core, keyed arm joints win at your priority.

local DAGGER_ARMS = {
    Idle = "rbxassetid://123456789",
    Walk = "rbxassetid://123456789",
    Run = "rbxassetid://123456789",
}

AnimSignals.LoadOverlay:Fire({
    Profile = "DaggerArms",
    Definition = DAGGER_ARMS,
    SetActive = true,
    Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action, -- always pass this
})

-- unequip
AnimSignals.SetOverlayProfile:Fire({ Profile = nil })

-- re-arm by name (definition remembered, active isn't)
AnimSignals.SetOverlayProfile:Fire({
    Profile = "DaggerArms",
    Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action,
})

Always pass Priority for overlays

Default comes from DefaultOverlayPriority (Core). Pass Action so keyed joints win and the rest falls through to core.

Overlay follows the active core slot-by-slot (run plays dagger-run, jump plays dagger-jump) and survives base profile swaps. Re-arm it each life via OnRigReady — see Death & Respawn.

Test it with WASD: AnimOverlayTest leaves the overlay on so you can eyeball arms-hold + walking legs.

docs.title: Quickstart (60 seconds)
docs.text:
One minute, three folders

Copy → suppress stock → fire a signal.

After this page you can swing an M1 and stop it mid-windup.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Roblox Studio (any place with an R15 or R6 rig)
  • This repo's Module/, Services/, Libraries/ folders

No Wally, no Rojo, no uploads. Tests run on Roblox's own public animations.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
Copy into StarterPlayerScripts, keeping the shape:

StarterPlayerScripts/
  Module/AnimateService        -- the engine (ModuleScript)
  Services/AnimateService      -- one-file launcher (LocalScript)
  Libraries/AnimSignals        -- typed signal bus (ModuleScript)
  Libraries/Signal             -- SignalPlus v3.7.2, vendored (ModuleScript)

Driving it from your own module loader instead? Skip Services/ and read Module Mode.

docs.title: 2. Kill stock Animate
docs.text:
Delete or disable Roblox's default Animate script in StarterPlayer > StarterCharacterScripts.

An empty Animate LocalScript suppresses it. The launcher does the rest.

docs.title: 3. (Optional) Give it legs
docs.text:
Add R15Animations and/or R6Animations folders as children of the Services/AnimateService script, each holding Animation objects named per slot:

Idle, Walk, Run, Sprint, Jump, Fall, Climb, Swim, SwimIdle, Sit

Stock-style StringValue slots work too. No folders at all is fine — the service runs combat-only and every Single still loads by asset id.

docs.title: 4. Swing something
docs.text:
From any LocalScript:

local AnimSignals = require(
    game.StarterPlayer.StarterPlayerScripts.Libraries.AnimSignals
)

-- snap into an M1 swing
AnimSignals.PlayCategoryTrack:Fire("M1", "rbxassetid://507766388", {
    FadeTime = 0.05,
    Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action2,
})

-- feint it 0.2s later
task.delay(0.2, function()
    AnimSignals.StopCategoryTrack:Fire("M1", "rbxassetid://507766388", 0.05)
end)

rbxassetid://507766388 is Roblox's default idle — it always loads, so you can test with zero uploads.

docs.title: 5. Prove it didn't leak
docs.text:
Copy Tests/ next to Services/ and Module/. Disable all but AnimValidator, press Play Solo:

[Validator] PASS single reuse second load flat -- before 10 mid 11 after 11
[Validator] PASS stop path alive
[Validator] PASS oneoff no permanent leak

Reset your character. You should see:

[Validator] PASS respawn rebuild == baseline -- got 10 want 10

Never 20, never 38. That's the whole promise.

docs.title: What you just got
docs.text:
• LoadedBin — that ID is now cached on your Animator. Fire it again and it replays in ~0.1ms.
  • Clean stop — StopCategoryTrack faded it out, no orphaned weight.
  • Per-life safety — reset and the track died with you. Fire again and it rebuilds warm.

Next: Life of a Swing — follow one M1 from button press to replay.

docs.title: Combat Recipes
docs.text: Copy-paste starters. Swap the IDs for your clips, keep the priorities.

docs.title: 1. M1 swing (kept Single)
docs.text:
local AnimSignals = require(path.to.Libraries.AnimSignals)
local M1_ID = "rbxassetid://123456789"

AnimSignals.PlayCategoryTrack:Fire("M1", M1_ID, {
    FadeTime = 0.05,
    Speed = 1.1,
    Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action2,
})

docs.title: 2. Skill with hitbox + shake markers
docs.text:
local SKILL_ID = "rbxassetid://123456789"

AnimSignals.BindMarker:Fire("Skill", SKILL_ID, "Hit", function()
    DamageService:CastHitbox()
end)

AnimSignals.BindMarker:Fire("Skill", SKILL_ID, "Impact", function()
    CameraShaker:Shake(CameraShaker.Presets.HeavyExplosion)
end)

AnimSignals.PlayCategoryTrack:Fire("Skill", SKILL_ID, {
    FadeTime = 0.1,
    Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action3,
})

docs.title: 3. Feint / dodge cancel
docs.text:
-- kill one swing
AnimSignals.StopCategoryTrack:Fire("M1", M1_ID, 0.05)

-- or kill ALL M1s at once
AnimSignals.StopCategoryTrack:Fire("M1", nil, 0.05)

docs.title: 4. Guard-broken / stunned
docs.text:
local HIT_ID = "rbxassetid://123456789"

AnimSignals.StopAllInCategory:Fire({ Category = "M1", Fade = 0.05 })
AnimSignals.StopAllInCategory:Fire({ Category = "Skill", Fade = 0.05 })

AnimSignals.PlayCategoryTrack:Fire("Stun", HIT_ID, {
    FadeTime = 0.05,
    Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action4,
})

docs.title: 5. Downslam finisher (auto-unload OneOff)
docs.text:
local SLAM_ID = "rbxassetid://123456789" -- needs a "hitreg" marker

AnimSignals.BindMarker:Fire("OneOff", SLAM_ID, "hitreg", function()
    SpawnGroundRubble()
end)

-- fire-and-forget: destroys itself the moment it stops
AnimSignals.PlayOneOff:Fire(SLAM_ID, { FadeTime = 0.05 })

docs.title: 6. Injured limp swap
docs.text:
-- below 25% HP ("Injured" loaded via LoadProfile or ExtraProfiles)
AnimSignals.SetCoreProfile:Fire({ Profile = "Injured" })

-- healed
AnimSignals.SetCoreProfile:Fire({ Profile = "__Default__" })

docs.title: 7. Custom core on demand, toggle with a key
docs.text:
Load lazily on first press — not at script top. Early fires vanish before the bus connects.

local FIST = {
    Idle = "rbxassetid://180435571",
    Walk = "rbxassetid://180426354",
    Run = "rbxassetid://180426354",
    Jump = "rbxassetid://125750702",
    Fall = "rbxassetid://180436148",
}

local fistLoaded, usingFist, db = false, false, false

uis.InputBegan:Connect(function(input, gameProcessed)
    if gameProcessed then return end
    if input.KeyCode ~= Enum.KeyCode.X or db then return end
    db = true
    usingFist = not usingFist
    if usingFist then
        if not fistLoaded then
            AnimSignals.LoadProfile:Fire({ Profile = "Fist", Definition = FIST, SetActive = true })
            fistLoaded = true
        else
            AnimSignals.SetCoreProfile:Fire({ Profile = "Fist" })
        end
    else
        AnimSignals.SetCoreProfile:Fire({ Profile = "__Default__" })
    end
    task.delay(0.3, function() db = false end)
end)

Once the service is running, LoadProfile, LoadOverlay and PreloadAnims are remembered even between lives. Play/stop/marker with no rig are dropped. SetCoreProfile to an unknown name warns instead of freezing.

docs.title: 8. Arms-layer overlay (Deepwoken pattern)
docs.text:
SetCoreProfile replaces locomotion. An overlay plays on top — arms-only clips for dagger stance or weapon guard — while combat Singles still override everything above it:

base core (__Default__) < overlay (arms, Action) < combat (M1/Skill, Action2+)

local DAGGER_ARMS = {
    Idle = "rbxassetid://123456789", -- arms-only, legs unkeyed!
    Walk = "rbxassetid://123456789",
    Run = "rbxassetid://123456789",
}

-- equip: load once, layer at Action so keyed joints win
AnimSignals.LoadOverlay:Fire({
    Profile = "DaggerArms",
    Definition = DAGGER_ARMS,
    SetActive = true,
    Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action,
})

-- unequip: base shows through, nothing reloaded
AnimSignals.SetOverlayProfile:Fire({ Profile = nil })

Overlay follows the active core slot-by-slot and survives base swaps. Its definition is remembered across respawns but the active overlay isn't — re-arm each life (see Death & Respawn).

docs.title: Signal Catalog (AnimSignals)
docs.text:
All communication happens through Libraries/AnimSignals.luau. Fire signals — never touch Animator:LoadAnimation() yourself.

Signal Payload When to fire PlayCategoryTrack (category: string, animId: string, opts?: PlayOpts) Attack, dash, block, skill. AutoPlay defaults true; false = load only. StopCategoryTrack (category: string, animId?: string, fade?: number) Feint, cancel, dodge windup. Omit animId = whole category. StopAllInCategory { Category: string, Fade?: number } Parried, stunned. Nuke a bucket. PlayOneOff (animId: string, opts?: PlayOpts) Finisher, execution, downslam. Self-destructs. BindMarker (category: string, animId: string, marker: string, cb) Hook hitbox / SFX / shake to a keyframe. ClearMarkers { Category: string, AnimId: string, Marker?: string } Drop listeners on cancel. Omit Marker = whole clip. SetCoreProfile { Profile: string } Stance / limp / class swap. Warns on unknown, never freezes. LoadProfile { Profile: string, Definition: { [string]: string }, SetActive?: boolean } Load a locomotion set from an id table. LoadOverlay { Profile: string, Definition: { [string]: string }, SetActive?: boolean, Priority?: Enum.AnimationPriority } Arms-layer set on top of core. SetOverlayProfile { Profile: string?, Priority?: Enum.AnimationPriority } Activate/clear overlay (nil clears). Pass Action. PreloadAnims { Ids: { string } } Pre-warm via ContentProvider pre-round. LoadBatch { Ids: { string }, Category?: string, Keep?: boolean } Equip moveset: preload + register without playing.

docs.title: Play options
docs.text:
type PlayOpts = {
    FadeTime: number?,  -- default 0.1
    Weight: number?,    -- default 1.0
    Speed: number?,     -- default 1.0
    Priority: Enum.AnimationPriority?, -- omitted = Core
    Looped: boolean?,
}

type LoadOptions = PlayOpts & {
    AutoPlay: boolean?, -- default true for PlayCategoryTrack/PlaySingle, false for LoadBatch
    Keep: boolean?,     -- reserved: stored, nothing reads it yet (no eviction)
    PreloadOnly: boolean?, -- register without Play()
    MarkerName: string?,
    MarkerCallback: ((...any) -> ())?,
    OnLoaded: ((AnimationTrack) -> ())?, -- cached or fresh: AdjustSpeed, TimePosition, etc.
}

Signals aren't queued

A fire before the bus connects — or between lives — vanishes. Load lazily once the service is up (see Recipes #7). Profiles, overlay defs and Preload are remembered; play/stop/marker with no rig are dropped.

docs.title: Quick fires
docs.text:
local AnimSignals = require(path.to.Libraries.AnimSignals)

-- play (loads if missing, reuses if present)
AnimSignals.PlayCategoryTrack:Fire("M1", M1_ID, {
    FadeTime = 0.05,
    Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action2,
})

-- load only
AnimSignals.PlayCategoryTrack:Fire("M1", M1_ID, { AutoPlay = false })

-- stop one swing / whole bucket / nuke + fade
AnimSignals.StopCategoryTrack:Fire("M1", M1_ID, 0.05)
AnimSignals.StopCategoryTrack:Fire("M1", nil, 0.05)
AnimSignals.StopAllInCategory:Fire({ Category = "M1", Fade = 0.05 })

-- one-off finisher (auto-destroys)
AnimSignals.PlayOneOff:Fire(SLAM_ID, { FadeTime = 0.05 })

-- markers
AnimSignals.BindMarker:Fire("Skill", SKILL_ID, "Hit", function()
    DamageService:CastHitbox()
end)
AnimSignals.ClearMarkers:Fire({ Category = "Skill", AnimId = SKILL_ID, Marker = "Hit" })

-- profiles & overlays
AnimSignals.LoadProfile:Fire({ Profile = "Injured", Definition = INJURED, SetActive = false })
AnimSignals.SetCoreProfile:Fire({ Profile = "Injured" })
AnimSignals.LoadOverlay:Fire({ Profile = "DaggerArms", Definition = ARMS, SetActive = true, Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action })
AnimSignals.SetOverlayProfile:Fire({ Profile = nil })

-- warmup
AnimSignals.PreloadAnims:Fire({ Ids = { M1_ID, SKILL_ID } })
AnimSignals.LoadBatch:Fire({ Ids = { M1_ID, SKILL_ID }, Category = "M1" })

docs.title: Tests & Studio Verification
docs.text: Nine proofs. All IDs are Roblox's own R15 defaults — no uploads needed. Run them one at a time in Play Solo (they share the character's bin).

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Tests/ next to Services/ + Module/ in StarterPlayerScripts.
  2. Toggle Disabled — only your target enabled.
  3. Play Solo, watch the client log.
  4. Swap IDs in Tests/TestKit.luau for your own clips whenever you like.

Marker checks need a clip with a real marker: set MarkerClip (and MarkerName) in TestKit, or those checks print SKIP.

# Script What it proves 1 AnimValidator Baseline count, reuse flat 10→11→11, marker path, stop path, OneOff no-leak, respawn rebuilds baseline 2 AnimStutterTest Raw LoadAnimation (~100ms+ hitch) vs PreloadAnims dispatch (~0.1ms) 3 AnimSingleTest Kept Singles persist across stop/replay, OneOff unloads, marker rubble (when MarkerClip set) 4 AnimPartialTest Stashed tracks die on respawn, sub-ms replay, Action vs Core WASD eyeball for partial-body 5 AnimOverlayTest Overlay layers at your priority, clearing stops it, re-arm by name works (leaves overlay on for WASD check) 6 AnimPersistCheck Runtime profile survives reset. Self-killing, runs once per session 7 AnimOneOffTest Warm OneOff dispatches without hitch and unloads itself 8 AnimMarkerTest Marker bookkeeping without a marked clip: handles, stacking, ClearMarkers by name + wholesale, signal parity. Needs Module/ + bus 9 AnimModuleTest Module mode with no signals: readiness, autoplay + reuse, stop, OneOff unload, static Preload, profile + OnRigReady survive respawn. Resets you — run alone

docs.title: Expected lines (spot-check)
docs.text:
[Validator] PASS single reuse second load flat -- before 10 mid 11 after 11
[Validator] PASS respawn rebuild == baseline -- got 10 want 10

[StutterTest] raw cold rbxassetid://50777xxxx content ready in 125.9ms
[StutterTest] service preloaded rbxassetid://50777xxxx dispatch took 0.1ms

[SingleTest] PASS kept single stays after stop
[SingleTest] SKIP marker reached -- set TestKit.Ids.MarkerClip ...

[PartialTest] CONFIRMED old track dead after respawn: parentNil=true replayOk=true
[PartialTest] ACTION priority: clip looped, WALK WITH WASD ... (8s)

[OverlayTest] PASS overlay sits at the requested Action
[PersistCheck] PASS respawn restores the last active profile
[OneOffTest] PASS no hitch after Preload -- 0.1ms
[MarkerTest] PASS two listeners stack -- count=2
[ModuleTest] PASS second PlayCategory reuses the track

AnimPartialTest, AnimPersistCheck and AnimModuleTest need a manual or automatic reset mid-run — that's intentional, they're testing death.

docs.title: Live inspect
docs.text:
Studio's Command Bar is server/edit — _G.__AnimateServiceDebug() there returns nil. Call it from any LocalScript (client log, or a debug script):

local fn = rawget(_G :: any, "__AnimateServiceDebug")
if typeof(fn) == "function" then
    local ok, info = pcall(fn)
    if ok then
        print("[AnimDebug] alive=", info.alive, "count=", info.count)
        for id, where in info.bin do
            print("  ", id, "->", where)
        end
    end
end

Module mode: AnimateService:GetDebugInfo() returns the same table. Config.Debug = false removes the global for release.

docs.title: Nothing plays
docs.text:
• Fired before Start? Early fires vanish. Load lazily once the service is up — not at script top.
  • Between lives? No rig = play/stop/marker dropped (nil). Use WaitForRig() / OnRigReady().
  • Unknown profile? SetCoreProfile to an unloaded name warns instead of freezing. LoadProfile first (or ExtraProfiles).
  • Stock Animate fighting you? Delete/disable it in StarterPlayer > StarterCharacterScripts. An empty Animate LocalScript suppresses it.

docs.title: Combat looks wrong
docs.text:
• Punch contends with legs? You omitted Priority (loads at Core). Pass Action2+ — or ClampCombatPriority = true.
  • Block jitters while walking? Same cause. Hands-only clips belong above locomotion. See Priority.
  • Legs frozen during guard? Your clip keys the legs. Leave lower torso + legs unkeyed for partial-body.
  • Stray Core clip stomping walk? Set LocomotionPriority = Movement.

docs.title: Markers never fire
docs.text:
• No marker in the clip? Checks print SKIP until you set MarkerClip/MarkerName in TestKit.
  • Bound after death? Listeners die with the character. Rebind each life, right before you play.
  • Move cancelled? ClearMarkers on feint/interrupt, or stale listeners pile on the reused track.

docs.title: OneOff won't unload / count grows
docs.text:
• OneOffs destroy on Stopped. If your clip loops (Looped = true), it never stops — force Looped = false for finishers.
  • Kept Singles intentionally stay till death (no eviction). That's not a leak — 10 → 11 → 11 is healthy. 10 → 20 after respawn is a leak (check you're not double-building rigs).

docs.title: Silent fails
docs.text:
• :Play() on a held track does nothing, no error? It died with the last character (Parent == nil). Dispatch by ID, never hoard tracks.
  • _G.__AnimateServiceDebug() is nil? You're in the server Command Bar. Call it from a LocalScript. Or Config.Debug = false shipped it away.

docs.title: Assets won't load
docs.text:
Clips you upload only load in experiences you own (or shared with). Tests use Roblox public defaults for that reason. BACKPACK-style ownership errors are Roblox telling you the asset isn't yours to play here.

Still stuck? Run AnimValidator alone and paste the full client log — it distinguishes reuse / stop / OneOff / respawn failures line by line.

docs.title: Config Reference
docs.text:
Pass to AnimateService:Configure() before Start(). Later calls only affect rigs built afterwards. UseSignals / Signals / Debug are read once at Start().

Key Default What it does UseSignals true Connect the AnimSignals bus. If none is found it's skipped quietly (direct-only). Signals auto Your AnimSignals table. Default searches script.Parent → grandparent → grandparent Libraries for an AnimSignals ModuleScript. Debug true Expose _G.__AnimateServiceDebug. Set false for release. CoreProfile nil Locomotion id table { Idle = "rbxassetid://…", Walk = … }. Wins over the next two. CoreResolver nil (Humanoid) -> ProfileDefinition? — pick by rig type or player data. CoreFolder the module Holds R15Animations / R6Animations or Animation objects. The launcher points it at itself. ExtraProfiles nil { [name]: ProfileDefinition } — loaded (not activated) every life so SetCoreProfile(name) works without LoadProfile first. PersistProfiles true Loaded profiles + active core survive respawns. LocomotionPriority Core Priority of locomotion tracks. Movement beats stray Core clips. ClampCombatPriority false Category tracks may only be Action2–Action4; anything lower (incl. Core/none) becomes MinCombatPriority. MinCombatPriority Action2 Clamp floor. DefaultOverlayPriority Core Overlay priority when the caller passes none. PlayingWarnThreshold 48 Warn past this many concurrent playing tracks (engine cap 64). Verbose false Lifecycle logging.

A combat game that keeps combat above locomotion:

AnimateService:Configure({
    CoreProfile = MyLocomotion,
    ExtraProfiles = { Injured = MyInjured },
    LocomotionPriority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Movement,
    ClampCombatPriority = true,
    DefaultOverlayPriority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action,
})

Launcher default (Services/AnimateService):

AnimateService:Configure({ CoreFolder = script })
AnimateService:Init()
AnimateService:Start()

docs.title: Controller API
docs.text: The LocalPlayer-facing service. All methods no-op / return nil between lives (no rig) — except preload/profile persistence, which are remembered.

docs.title: Readiness
docs.text:
Method Signature Notes IsReady () -> boolean rig ~= nil GetRig () -> Rig? Never cache across respawn — ask again WaitForRig (timeout?: number) -> Rig? Yields until spawn (or timeout → nil) OnRigReady (cb: (Rig) -> ()) -> Connection Fires now if a rig exists + every respawn. SignalPlus Connection (:Disconnect()) 
local rig = AnimateService:WaitForRig(10)
local conn = AnimateService:OnRigReady(function(rig)
    -- re-arm overlays, rebind markers
end)

docs.title: Playback
docs.text: Method Signals equivalent PlayCategory(category, animId, opts?: LoadOptions): AnimationTrack? PlayCategoryTrack (AutoPlay defaults true; false = load only) PlayOneOff(animId, opts?: PlayOpts): AnimationTrack? PlayOneOff (forces Looped = false, auto-destroys on Stopped) StopCategory(category, animId?: string, fade?: number) StopCategoryTrack StopAllCategory(category, fade?: number) StopAllInCategory

docs.title: Markers
docs.text:
Method Signals equivalent OnMarker(category, animId, marker, cb): MarkerHandle? BindMarker ClearMarkers(category, animId, marker?) ClearMarkers (nil = whole clip)

MarkerHandle = { Connected: boolean, Disconnect: (self) -> () }.

docs.title: Queries
docs.text:
• GetTrack(category, animId): AnimationTrack?
  • IsPlaying(category, animId): boolean
  • GetLoadedCount(): number
  • GetLoadedList(): { [cleanId]: "category/Kind" }
  • GetDebugInfo(): { alive, count, bin, animatorPlaying, profiles }
  • SetLocomotionWeight(mult, fade?) — scale active locomotion weight.

Live inspect from any LocalScript:

local fn = rawget(_G :: any, "__AnimateServiceDebug")
local ok, info = pcall(fn)
if ok then
    print("[AnimDebug] alive=", info.alive, "count=", info.count)
    for id, where in info.bin do print("  ", id, "->", where) end
end

Config.Debug = false removes the global for release.

docs.title: Preload (works with no rig)
docs.text:
• Preload(ids: { string }) — ContentProvider warmup. Call from a loading screen.
  • LoadBatch(ids, category?: string, keep?: boolean?) — preload + LoadCategory(category or "Single", id, { AutoPlay = false }).

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
• SetCoreProfile(name) — activate (persists if PersistProfiles).
  • LoadProfile(name, def, setActive?: boolean) — setActive ~= false also activates. Existing names ignored.
  • ReplaceProfile(name, def) — swap contents of an existing profile.
  • LoadOverlay(name, def, setActive?, priority?) — definition persisted, active overlay not.
  • SetOverlayProfile(name?, priority?) — nil clears.
  • ClearOverlay().

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
• Configure(opts: Config) — shallow-merge. Call before Start for first life; later calls affect rigs built after.
  • Init() — idempotent. Warns + disables on server (use Rig.new there).
  • Start() — connects signals, exposes debug, hooks CharacterAdded, builds current rig.
  • Shutdown() — test helper. Destroys rig, disconnects signals, forgets persisted profiles, removes _G hook.

docs.title: Rig API
docs.text:
The per-life workhorse. AnimateService.Rig.new(model) works on any Humanoid rig (NPCs untested but structurally supported). The controller owns one for your LocalPlayer automatically.

local rig = AnimateService.Rig.new(model)
rig:LoadProfile("__Default__", def)
rig:SetActiveProfile("__Default__")
rig:Init()
rig:Start()
-- later: rig:Destroy()

Constructor stops + destroys leftover engine tracks, waits for Humanoid / Animator.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
• HasProfile(name): boolean
  • LoadProfile(name, def): Rig — skips if destroyed / exists. SwimIdle normalised, Priority = LocomotionPriority, Looped = (name ~= "Jump").
  • SetActiveProfile(name?): Rig — nil → last loaded. Warns on unknown. Stops active tracks, re-evaluates.
  • ChangeAll(name, def): Rig — destroy old record + reload (used by ReplaceProfile).

docs.title: Playback
docs.text:
• PlaySingle(category, animId, opts?: PlayOpts): AnimationTrack? — LoadCategory with AutoPlay = true.
  • PlayOneOff(animId, opts?: PlayOpts): AnimationTrack? — category = "OneOff", Looped = false, Stopped:Once → destroy.
  • LoadCategory(category, animId, opts?: LoadOptions): AnimationTrack? — three-tier lookup (same-bucket → _byId share → fresh LoadAnimation), honouring AutoPlay / PreloadOnly / Priority / Looped / MarkerName+Callback / OnLoaded.
  • StopCategory(category, animId?: string, fade?: number) — default fade 0.05.
  • StopAllCategory(category, fade?).
  • Preload(ids: { string }) — no-op if destroyed. Deduped process-wide.

docs.title: Markers
docs.text:
• OnMarker(category, animId, marker, cb): MarkerHandle? — lazy-loads (AutoPlay = false) on miss. One native conn per marker, fanout via task.spawn.
  • ClearMarkers(category, animId, marker?).
  • GetMarkerListenerCount(category, animId, marker): number.

Non-looped category tracks get an automatic Ended → Stop(0.05) so one-shots end for everyone.

docs.title: Queries
docs.text:
• GetTrack(category, animId): AnimationTrack?
  • IsPlaying(category, animId): boolean
  • GetLoadedCount(): number
  • GetLoadedList(): { [cleanId]: string }
  • GetProfileCount(): number
  • GetAnimatorPlayingCount(): number (pcall(GetPlayingAnimationTracks))

docs.title: Locomotion tuning
docs.text:
• SetLocomotionWeight(mult, fade?) — scale _activeTracks weight.
  • ChangeAnimateParams(patch) — raw thresholds/dividends: SprintThreshold = 24, RunThreshold = 17, WalkThreshold = 0.01, SprintDividend = 22, RunDividend = 18, WalkDividend = 16, ClimbDividend = 12, SwimDividend = 16, JumpDuration = 0.31, ApplyRigScale = true.

_speed() = horizontal HumanoidRootPart.AssemblyLinearVelocity magnitude / Character:GetScale() when ApplyRigScale.

State map (Running / Climbing / Swimming(speed), StateChanged, Died):

State Track Dead / GettingUp / FallingDown / PlatformStanding / Physics stop all core + overlay Seated Sit (0.5) FreeFalling (and not mid-jump) Fall (0.3) Climbing Climb (0.1, speed/12) Swimming speed < 5 → SwimIdle (0.2) else Swim (0.3, speed/16) Jumping Jump (0.1) Running + still Idle (0.1) speed >= 24 Sprint (0.2, speed/22) speed >= 17 Run (0.2, speed/18) speed > 0.01 Walk (0.15, speed/16) else Idle (0.1)

docs.title: Overlays
docs.text:
• SetOverlayProfile(name?, priority?): Rig — re-evaluates if running.
  • ClearOverlay(): Rig.

Overlay plays in lockstep after every core track (_playOverlayAnim at the end of _playProfileAnim), same FadeTime/Speed, priority = passed or DefaultOverlayPriority.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
• Init(): Rig — connects StateChanged / Running / Climbing / Swimming / Died.
  • Start(): Rig — seeds state, evaluates once.
  • Destroy() — disconnect all, destroy active + profile + category tracks, clear markers/EndStopConn, reset counts.
